I’ve farmed these 16 mu for 40 years, just me and my wife now. The wheat is already in the ground from last October — I sowed Jinmai 47, about 25 jin per mu. It’s an improved variety, not the fanciest hybrid, but it’s reliable. Last year I got about 480 kg per mu. For fertilizer, the input dealer told me 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I’ve always done a bit more to be safe. I put half a bag of compound fertilizer down as base at sowing, and now in spring I’ll top-dress with urea — about 40 jin at green-up and another 20 jin at jointing. That works out to about 18 kg nitrogen per mu total, plus 7 kg phosphorus and 6 kg potassium from the compound. I irrigate three times: green-up water in March, jointing in April, and heading in May. Pumping costs money, but a dry spell at heading will kill your yield. I spray twice for aphids and powdery mildew.

After wheat harvest in early June, I plant summer maize on that same 12 mu. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — my neighbor Lao Wang switched to it three years ago and his yields went up, so I did too. I buy about 4 jin of seed per mu. Time is tight after wheat harvest, only a few days, so I no-till plant straight into the stubble. Base fertilizer is compound, about 80 jin per mu, then I top-dress urea at big trumpet stage — about 30 jin. That’s about 17 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. Maize needs less water than wheat — twice is usually enough, at jointing and grain filling. Two sprays for corn borer.

The other 4.1 mu is cotton. I plant Bt hybrid cotton in late April. Cotton needs more care. Base fertilizer is compound plus some extra potassium sulfate because cotton likes potassium for the bolls. Total nitrogen about 14 kg per mu, phosphorus 5 kg, potassium 8 kg. I irrigate three times and spray five times — aphids, spider mites, and bollworm even with Bt cotton. I do rotary tillage for cotton since I have time in spring.

Everything costs more this year. Fertilizer prices went up again. But I’m 62, I can’t afford a bad year. I’d rather put down a bit too much than risk losing yield. Last year I spent heavy on inputs and still came out okay. My neighbor uses about the same amounts, and he always does alright. That’s good enough for me.
